dataThroughRule: Capture date in Pacific time (2026-10-08) minus 3 days, the same processing delay the repository's own date-window helper uses (scripts/agents/seo/lib/date-windows.ts, processingDelayDays=3). Search Console does not print its final-data date, so this is an assumption, not a Google statement.

notes: Captured from the property owner's signed-in Search Console session in the Claude desktop built-in browser (Hebrew UI). Read-only: no export download, no Request Indexing, no URL live test, no sitemap action.

Tables were read from the rendered page text; each CSV reproduces the Search Console export layout. Row counts, click totals and daily sums were cross-checked against the report headers (see capture-notes.md).
dates-recent lists 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-08 as zero-impression days; those days are after dataThrough (2026-10-05) and are not final, so the importer marks them non-final rather than measured zeros.

Query tables are marked private: the repository is public and keeps query-level data outside git (see docs/growth/receipts/20260925-first-revenue/README.md). Copies live under ~/MilooshReceipts/20261009-growth-agent-system/gsc-ui-capture-20261009/.

Page-level query tables (queries-page-software-*) were read for the five pages the Director shortlisted, with the report filtered to 'Page contains /software/<slug>' for the historical window. Each table's impression total equals that page's row in pages-historical.csv, which is how the importer decides to attribute it. Search Console lists only queries it does not anonymise; the remaining impressions are not listed. They are private for the same reason as the other query tables.

Exact-page checks: the same five pages, recent window 2026-09-08..2026-10-05, the same filter, returned 0 clicks and 0 impressions. Because the filter is 'contains', it also covers the www host and any URL starting with the same path.
